premises: At S5, the provider guarantees the returned attempt history is complete for exact O5,D5,I5.
Every attempt present in the complete S5 history reports started=false.
The provider does not guarantee S5 is sealed, terminal, or quiescent.
A future retry or later execution for O5,D5,I5 may still be created after S5.
No provider-level terminal no-more-attempts attestation is available.
Repository finalization still requires current F5 claim/predecessor CAS and exact readback.
fixture.candidate_action: F5 records terminal negative/non-effect closure from complete-at-S5 all-started=false history plus current-claim CAS/readback.
fixture.reason: Snapshot completeness proves only that no covered attempt had started up to S5. Because the history is explicitly unsealed, the logical operation can still acquire a later retry or execution after the negative closure is committed. Repository fencing/CAS can serialize the repository transition, but it cannot by itself make the provider history terminal or prevent a delayed provider-side attempt from crossing the effect boundary. Terminal negative closure therefore requires both completeness for the relevant identity and a quiescence/sealing property that excludes future execution, or an equivalent provider-side terminalization primitive bound to the same identity.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: For exact O5,D5,I5, a provider-guaranteed complete current attempt-history snapshot in which every attempt reports started=false, combined with current F5 CAS/readback, is sufficient to record terminal non-effect closure even if future attempts remain possible.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: The rule is unsafe because completeness is time-bounded to S5 while terminal closure is a statement about the future as well as the past. A retry created after S5 can still start or produce an irreversible effect unless a separate sealing/quiescence guarantee prevents it.

required_properties: Exact binding of the proof to O5,D5,I5.
Complete history for all attempts relevant to the identity up to the terminalization point.
Sealed/terminal quiescence: no new attempt for O5,D5,I5 can be created, resumed, or executed after the proof is issued.
For every covered attempt, started=false must semantically exclude crossing the irreversible-effect boundary, or an equivalent explicit no-effect attestation must be supplied.
minimum_additional_provider_evidence.repository_side_guard_after_provider_pro: Only after provider-side completeness and sealing/quiescence are both established may current F5 CAS plus exact readback safely finalize terminal negative closure in repository state.

observations: Completeness and sealing are distinct proof obligations: a history can be complete at a snapshot while remaining open to future attempts.
All-started=false across a complete current snapshot establishes no-start for the past covered set, not impossibility of future start.
Repository fencing protects repository authority and duplicate finalization, but does not synthesize provider-side terminality.
inference: Within this exact fixture, completeness without terminal quiescence is still insufficient for terminal negative/non-effect closure. The minimal safe proof must combine identity-bound complete history with a sealing/quiescence guarantee, or use an equivalent atomic provider terminalization primitive that prevents later execution for the same idempotency identity.
